contentTypes.name: Short (2 to 3 minutes) content promoting an upcoming theatrical feature.
Very short (typically less than 1 minute) content promoting an upcoming theatrical feature.
Content used to test, calibrate or setup D-Cinema exhibition equipment.
Slate/still picture indicating the recommended age group permitted to view the content to follow. This rating is generally unique per country.
Content promoting a product or service other than an upcoming feature.
Non advertising/promotional content (3 to 15 minutes) typically before a theatrical feature.
Extremely short content (1 to 15 seconds) separating unrelated compositions.
Content defining the code of conduct for patrons.
An excerpt from a longer piece of content that may be displayed on its own or with other clips.
A piece of promotional publicity or advertising.
'Please Put Your 3D Glasses On Now' card
Part of a dramatic work such as a serial television program.
Edited sequence of one or more memorable parts of an event, feature, episode or period of time.
Activity that happens at a given place and time, especially one of importance, including a music performance, a contest making up a sports competition.

contentModifiers.name: Indicates the version number of the Composition.

Final composition, including final sound, picture and accessibility features. Note: You should not use this modifier code in the CTT - this is present only to show the intended value of the VersionNumber's 'status' attribute in a 'Final' Composition.
Temporary composition, e.g. preview or rough-cut version. Picture and/or sound are temporary and unfinished.
Pre-release Composition. Picture and sound are final, but not all features of the final version such as accessibility features are present.

For US released trailers, NATO and the MPAA have requested that trailers with the Red Band MPAA rating be clearly marked early in the DCP file name. This is so theatres will more clearly see the trailer is restricted, and not accidently place a Red Band trailer with a G, PG, or PG-13 movie.
A human-readable name of the specific targeted use (specific theatre chain or event) for which the Composition Playlist is intended.
Alternative version - You have the option of using the word 'ALT' in the theatre chain sub-field instead of naming a specific theatre chain or event.
If the product is in both 2D and 3D, label the 2D version: '2D'. If the product only exists in 2D, you do not need to label it '2D' - it will be assumed to be in 2D if it is not otherwise described.

There is currently no luminance standard for mastering 3D content. Some films are color timed at 3.5 foot lamberts, others at 4, 4.5, 6, 7, and even 10 foot lamberts. If you have multiple luminance versions of your product, put the foot lamberts numerical value here in order to signal which version the DCP contains. Do not use decimal points for the CTT.
Frame Rate numerical value (if other than 24 frames per second).
Identifies content that is intended for playback on theater screens that are part of the "Infinity Vision" program (https://www.infinityvisiontickets.com).
